title: Redesign adaptive assistive row for form fields: layout, density, and multi-line behavior
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: The current helper/affix/error row beneath inputs is brittle across density modes and multi-line controls (autosize textareas, multi-select chips). In high-density views helper text collides with counters or icons; in localized builds long helper strings break layout; and validation messages are not consistently surfaced to ATs. Goal: produce an adaptive assistive row component that composes helper text, character counters, status icons, validation messages, and optional action affordances in a predictable, accessible, and token-driven layout.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: single-line and multi-line text inputs, selects with chips, number fields, and autosize textarea behaviors. Layout rules, token mappings for spacing/typography, aria relationships, and animations for appearing validation.
- Out of scope for this ticket: redesign of checkbox/radio groups, new validation rule engine, or backend validation APIs. Those are follow-ups tied to ENG-9002.

Design principles and decisions to make:
1) Single-row-first semantics: when space permits, helpers + counter + small status icon live in one row. When not, validation takes priority and pushes helper text to a second row.
2) Density-driven tokenization: spacing and type scale must be derived from density tokens (compact / default / roomy) instead of hard-coded px. This ensures parity across themes and future density additions.
3) Predictable overflow: helper text truncates with an inline ellipsis accompanied by a tooltip on hover/focus; validation messages never truncate and stack below.
4) i18n & RTL: measure for long translations and RTL icon flipping. Design must support up to 40% longer strings without layout breakage.
5) A11y: validation messages should be announced via aria-live polite for non-blocking warnings and assertive for errors; inputs must maintain aria-describedby pointing to visible helper/validation IDs.
6) Motion: use a short CSS transition for validation arrival (fade + vertical micro-shift) that respects reduced motion settings.

Acceptance criteria:
- New assistive row component prototypes exist in Figma for compact/default/roomy densities and for single-line and stacked modes.
- Token spec created mapping: helper-row-gap, helper-row-font-size, helper-row-line-height, helper-row-icon-gap.
- Accessibility checklist completed (aria-describedby, aria-live mapping, keyboard tooltip triggers).
- Interaction spec for chunking behavior (when counter and helper conflict) and rules for when helper collapses to tooltip.
- Responsive tests: examples for 320px, 480px, 768px widths demonstrating behavior.
- Engineering-ready documentation with CSS variables and recommended React props (maxHelperChars, preferStacking, statusPriority).

Deliverables:
- Figma components and variants (desktop + mobile), plus component spec tokens.
- A short prototype (storybook) demonstrating all states: idle, focused, helper overflow, warning, error, multi-line wrap, i18n long strings, RTL.
- PRD section describing developer API and migration notes for existing inputs.

Edge cases and trade-offs:
- Preferring stacked validation messages improves clarity but increases vertical rhythm cost; for compact density we default to tooltip for helper text instead of stacking to preserve vertical density.
- Counters are less critical than errors; design enforces a statusPriority order: error > warning > helper/counter.
- Tooltips introduce discovery friction on touch devices; add long-press reveal for mobile.

Testing and QA:
- Manual QA list for designers and engineers including NVDA/VoiceOver tests for announcements, character counter updates on input, screen reader focus behavior on validation, and RTL checks.
- Automated visual snapshots for critical states and a11y linting rules in CI.

Implementation notes for Eng team (high level):
- Provide stable ID generation for aria-describedby so descriptors can be targeted consistently across re-renders.
- Expose a small API surface: descriptorNodes: { helperId, counterId, validationId }, preferStacking boolean, density token prop.
- Use CSS variables for token overrides so runtime density toggles don't require component re-render.

Migration plan:
1) Create assistive-row component and ship behind a feature flag.
2) Migrate high-traffic form fields (signup, payments) first with A/B telemetry to monitor error recognition and layout regressions.
3) Gradual rollout with toggle for backfilling older screens.

Success metrics:
- Reduced layout shift incidents in console (tracking layout-CLS-like metric for forms) by 40% on pages migrated.
- Reduction in user-reported validation confusion in support tickets by 25% for migrated flows.
- No critical accessibility regressions detected in automated audits.

Notes: coordinate with ENG-8421 for aria-live implementation details and PM-412 for rollout prioritization.
